children.title: Basis Repair Safeguard
children.top_down_role: Corrective replacement or adjustment of an unreliable basis state.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Repair Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local column-exchange repair of an invalid or numerically unacceptable simplex basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a basis index set \(T\), its factorization, and thresholds \(\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}>0\) and \(\varepsilon_p\ge0\). Identify a basic row or column responsible for a rank warning, bound violation, or unstable solve. Among eligible nonbasic columns, select \(j\notin T\) and a leaving index \(i\in T\) such that the normalized pivot magnitude is at least \(\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\). Form \(T'=(T\setminus\{i\})\cup\{j\}\), update the factorization, and recompute original-data residuals. Retain \(T'\) only if \(A_{T'}\) is nonsingular and the designated defect decreases without making primal violation exceed its acceptance rule; otherwise undo the exchange and escalate to reinversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair a suspect basis by one stable column exchange, retaining the change only when nonsingularity and original-data residual checks improve.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(|T|=m\).
An eligible entering column and leaving position can be tested.
The previous basis state is retained for rollback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T'\text{ is retained only if }A_{T'}\text{ is nonsingular and the acceptance checks pass}.\)

notation.meaning: old and repaired basis index sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the basis-repair leaf, but the normalized pivot test, defect-decrease criterion, rollback rule, and escalation policy are implementation-specific and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Basis Reinversion Safeguard
children.top_down_role: Fresh basis-factor construction used to discard accumulated update error.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Reinversion Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fresh factorization and residual validation of the current basis matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a basis index set \(T\), discard accumulated product-form or update factors and assemble \(B=A_T\) from the original constraint matrix. Compute a fresh rank-revealing factorization of \(B\). If numerical rank is less than \(m\), report the basis as singular and invoke basis repair. Otherwise solve anew for the basic primal variables and simplex multipliers, recompute primal and dual residuals from the original data, and replace the old factors only when the factorization residual and both solve residuals satisfy their prescribed thresholds. The accepted output is the unchanged combinatorial basis \(T\) with a newly validated factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rebuild the current basis factorization from original columns, reject numerical singularity, and accept fresh factors only after independent residual checks.
assumptions_latex: \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) has cardinality \(m\).
Original matrix columns and problem data are available.
Rank and residual thresholds are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{output}=(T,\text{fresh factors})\) only after rank and residual validation.

notation.meaning: basis matrix assembled from original columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and local subject are appropriate, but the rank-revealing factorization choice and the three residual acceptance thresholds require an authoritative numerical linear algebra or simplex implementation source.

children.title: Repair-versus-Reinversion Trigger
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic boundary separating structural basis repair from numerical reinversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair-versus-Reinversion Trigger
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic rule selecting local basis exchange or fresh numerical factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_f\) measure the residual of the maintained basis factorization, let \(r_s\) measure the associated linear-solve residual, and let \(d_T\) indicate a structural basis defect such as numerical rank loss or absence of an admissible stable pivot. With fixed thresholds \(\eta_f,\eta_s\ge0\), trigger reinversion when \(r_f>\eta_f\) or \(r_s>\eta_s\) while the current basis columns remain structurally admissible. Trigger basis repair when \(d_T=1\), including when fresh reinversion confirms rank deficiency. If both diagnostics fire, reinvert first to distinguish accumulated factorization error from a genuine combinatorial basis defect, then repair only if the defect persists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reinvert for stale numerical factors; repair for a persistent structural basis defect. When uncertain, fresh factorization diagnoses which action is necessary.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are computed using original matrix data.
\(\eta_f\) and \(\eta_s\) are scaled consistently.
Repair supports rollback after an unsuccessful exchange.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_f>\eta_f\ \vee\ r_s>\eta_s\Rightarrow\text{reinvert};\qquad d_T=1\text{ after reinversion}\Rightarrow\text{repair}.\)

notation.meaning: indicator of a persistent structural basis defect

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the trigger leaf, but the prescribed decision rule and mandatory reinvert-first ordering are solver-specific policies with no supporting source.

knowledge_statements.title: Spanning-Tree Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-simplex basis for a connected capacitated flow network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected directed graph and let \(A\) be its node-arc incidence matrix with one row deleted. An arc set \(T\subseteq E\) is a spanning-tree basis when \(|T|=|V|-1\) and the undirected edges underlying \(T\) form a connected acyclic graph on \(V\). Equivalently, the square reduced incidence submatrix \(A_T\) is nonsingular. Arc orientations do not affect this basis characterization; they only determine the signs of entries in \(A_T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tree Arc Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic-arc component of a bounded network-simplex state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a connected capacitated network \(G=(V,E)\), a tree arc set is a subset \(T\subseteq E\) whose underlying undirected edges form a spanning tree of \(V\). Thus \(|T|=|V|-1\), and after deleting any one incidence row, the submatrix \(A_T\) is square and nonsingular. In a network-simplex state, flows on arcs in \(T\) are the basic variables and are determined by flow conservation after all non-tree arc flows have been fixed at their designated bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplex method for uncapacitated network flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One primal network-simplex iteration from a feasible tree solution, including its stopping outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Start from a basic feasible flow }\mathbf f\text{ with tree }T.\text{ Compute node prices }\mathbf p\text{ along the rooted tree and }\bar c_{ij}=c_{ij}-(p_i-p_j)\text{ for }(i,j)\notin T.\text{ If every }\bar c_{ij}\geq0,\text{ terminate with an optimal flow. Otherwise choose }(i,j)\notin T\text{ with }\bar c_{ij}<0.\text{ Adding it to }T\text{ creates a unique cycle. Let }B\text{ be the cycle arcs oriented opposite to }(i,j).\text{ If }B=\varnothing,\text{ the optimal value is }-\infty.\text{ Otherwise set }\theta^*=\min_{(k,\ell)\in B}f_{k\ell},\text{ augment }\theta^*\text{ around the cycle, and remove an old basic arc whose resulting flow is zero}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible tree flow, compute tree-induced node prices and the reduced costs of non-tree arcs. Nonnegative reduced costs certify optimality. Otherwise insert a negative-reduced-cost arc, augment around its unique fundamental cycle, and remove a tree arc that reaches zero. If the cycle has no oppositely oriented arc, the objective is unbounded below.

\text{the network-flow problem is uncapacitated}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The iteration either certifies optimality, detects optimal value }-\infty,\text{ or produces a new basic feasible tree solution}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A network-simplex arc-status triple \((T,L,U)\) is partition-consistent when \[E=T\mathbin{\dot\cup}L\mathbin{\dot\cup}U,\qquad |T|=|V|-1,\qquad T\text{ spans }V,\] and its state vector satisfies \(x_e=l_e\) for every \(e\in L\) and \(x_e=u_e\) for every \(e\in U\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of network basis states by a tree and bound statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be connected, let \(A\) be its incidence matrix with one row removed, and consider \(Ax=b\) with \(l\le x\le u\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a primal-feasible tree-flow state and compute tree-compatible potentials. Select a non-tree arc at its lower bound with \(\bar c_e<0\), using direction \(z^e\), or an arc at its upper bound with \(\bar c_e>0\), using direction \(-z^e\). Increase \(\theta\ge0\) maximally while \(\ell\le x+\theta d\le u\), where \(d\) is the selected direction. If no finite maximum exists, the improving circulation certifies unboundedness. Otherwise choose a blocking arc, update the tree and bound statuses, and recompute the affected state. Stop when no non-tree arc violates its bound-dependent reduced-cost sign; the resulting state satisfies the network-basis optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal network simplex preserves feasible flows while pivoting along improving fundamental cycles until reduced-cost signs certify optimality, or an unlimited improving cycle certifies unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Network Simplex

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a tree basis whose non-tree reduced costs satisfy their bound-dependent dual signs. If every tree flow lies in its interval, stop with an optimal basis. Otherwise choose a tree arc \(t\) violating a bound and delete it to form \(D_t\). Change the potential difference between the two shores until an eligible non-tree arc crossing \(D_t\) first attains zero reduced cost; choose that arc by the dual ratio test. Insert it, move \(t\) to the bound selected by its violation, and recompute the tree flow. Repeat while preserving all non-tree reduced-cost signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual network simplex repairs bound-infeasible tree flows through cut pivots while retaining reduced-cost feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Network Simplex

source_refs.locator: 9.1 The Minimal Cost Network Flow Problem p. 453

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(y=x-\ell\) and \(b'=b-A\ell\). Then \[Ay=b',\qquad y\ge0.\] Apply network-simplex pivots to \(y\) with the original cost vector, since \(c^{\mathsf T}x=c^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}\ell\). If finite upper bounds \(u\) are also present, impose \(y_e\le u_e-\ell_e\). On termination return \(x=y+\ell\). This affine transformation preserves feasibility, improving directions, and optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting finite lower bounds converts the problem to nonnegative flows with shifted balances, after which network simplex applies.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bounded Network Simplex

knowledge_statements.title: Opposite-Bound Arc Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-flip case of the two-sided bounded network-simplex pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Add \(e\) to \(T\), orient the resulting fundamental cycle \(C_e\) in the improving residual direction of \(e\), and increase the residual flow uniformly around \(C_e\). Let \(\theta\) be the minimum residual capacity among its directed cycle arcs. If no tree arc blocks at \(\theta\) and the residual capacity of \(e\) is \(\theta=u_e-\ell_e\), augment by \(\theta\), retain the same tree \(T\), and change the status of \(e\) from its current bound to the opposite bound. No tree arc leaves the basis in this transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the entering arc reaches its opposite bound without any tree arc blocking at the same step, flip its nonbasic bound status and leave the spanning tree unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The minimum-cost flow problem has finite bounds \(\ell_a\le x_a\le u_a\) and a primal-feasible tree basis \(T\).
The entering nonbasic arc \(e\) is directed in its improving residual direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(e\) reaches its opposite bound at \(\theta=u_e-\ell_e\) and no tree arc blocks at \(\theta\), then \(T\) is unchanged and \(e\) becomes nonbasic at its opposite bound.

notation.meaning: fundamental cycle formed by adding arc e to T

knowledge_statements.title: Entering-Arc Pricing Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal network-simplex pricing for a minimization problem with two-sided bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonbasic arc define the signed improvement measure by \(s_a=\bar c_a\) for \(a\in L\) and \(s_a=-\bar c_a\) for \(a\in U\). An arc is eligible exactly when \(s_a<0\). A pricing family specifies how eligible arcs are searched or ranked: examples include first eligible, minimum \(s_a\), cyclic search, and partial or candidate-list pricing. Return a selected eligible arc as the entering arc. If no eligible arc exists, return the optimality certificate \(s_a\ge 0\) for every nonbasic arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing searches lower- and upper-bound nonbasic arcs using signed reduced costs, selecting an improving arc or certifying reduced-cost optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental-Cycle Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycle update for a bounded minimum-cost-flow tree basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Insert \(e\) into \(T\), producing the unique cycle \(C_e\). Orient \(C_e\) in the residual direction of \(e\), and define \(d^e_a=1\) on forward cycle arcs, \(d^e_a=-1\) on reverse cycle arcs, and \(d^e_a=0\) otherwise. Set \(x(\alpha)=x+\alpha d^e\) and compute \(\theta=\max\{\alpha\ge 0:\ell_a\le x_a(\alpha)\le u_a\text{ for every }a\in A\}\). Augment to \(x'=x(\theta)\). Since \(d^e\) is a circulation, the node-balance equations are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an entering arc creates one cycle; augmenting uniformly around it preserves balances until the first arc bound is reached.
assumptions_latex: The directed network has arc set \(A\), finite bounds \(\ell_a\le u_a\) for every \(a\in A\), and a feasible flow \(x\).
The tree arcs \(T\subseteq A\) form a spanning tree, and \(x\) satisfies the node-balance equations.
A nonbasic arc \(e\in A\setminus T\) is chosen with an improving residual direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated flow remains balanced and is feasible for every \(0\le\alpha\le\theta\).

notation.meaning: fundamental cycle of e relative to T

If \(B_\theta\setminus\{e\}\neq\varnothing\), choose a tree arc \(f\in B_\theta\setminus\{e\}\) by the prescribed deterministic tie-breaking rule, declare \(f\) nonbasic at the bound it attains, and declare \(e\) basic. If \(B_\theta=\{e\}\), perform an opposite-bound transition instead. When \(\theta=0\), the same selection rule defines a degenerate pivot without changing the flow.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding \(e\) to \(T\) creates exactly one fundamental cycle \(C_e\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the maximum feasible cycle step is \(\theta=0\), at least one tree arc already at a bound blocks the entering direction. Selecting such an arc to leave and applying the tree exchange gives \(x'=x+\theta d^e=x\), hence the primal objective is unchanged. Nevertheless, \(T'=(T\cup\{e\})\setminus\{f\}\) may differ from \(T\), and the nonbasic statuses, potentials, and subsequent eligible arcs may change. Thus a zero-augmentation pivot is algebraically degenerate but remains a genuine transition between network-basis states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-step pivot changes the tree basis and related state but leaves the feasible flow and its objective value unchanged.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly feasible trees and lexicographic positivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-simplex bases represented by feasible rooted spanning trees, including a root arc whose flow is always zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible rooted basis tree is strongly feasible if every degenerate nonroot basic arc is directed toward the root; equivalently, for each such arc \((i,j)\), one has \(j=p(i)\). A basis \(B\) corresponds to a strongly feasible tree if and only if every row of \([B^{-1}b,\,B^{-1}]\) is lexicographically positive. Consequently, a network-simplex scheme that maintains strongly feasible trees terminates after finitely many pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible rooted basis tree is strongly feasible when every zero-flow nonroot basic arc points toward the root. Such trees are exactly the bases whose rows in the augmented inverse-basis array are lexicographically positive; maintaining them guarantees finite network-simplex termination.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ is a feasible network-simplex basis represented by a rooted spanning tree}
\text{the root arc is included and has zero flow in every feasible solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is strongly feasible}\iff [B^{-1}b,\,B^{-1}]\text{ has lexicographically positive rows},\qquad \text{and maintaining this property implies finite termination}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction of an initial strongly feasible basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization of a network-simplex basis from either an all-artificial basis or an advanced feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an all-artificial starting basis, direct every artificial arc incident to a transshipment node toward the dummy root. For an advanced feasible basis, choose a root and form the spanning forest of positive-flow arcs. If it is connected, it is already strongly feasible. Otherwise, repeatedly join a component not containing the root to the root component by an available arc directed from the former to the latter; every added arc is degenerate. If no such arc exists from the unconnected set \(X\) to \(\bar X\), then \(\sum_{i\in X}b_i=\sum_{i\in\bar X}b_i=0\), every arc from \(\bar X\) to \(X\) has zero flow in every feasible solution, and the problem separates over \(X\) and \(\bar X\). One may then solve the components independently or connect \(X\) to the root with a degenerate artificial arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An all-artificial basis becomes strongly feasible by orienting its artificial arcs toward the dummy root. From an advanced feasible basis, connect the components of the positive-flow forest toward the root using degenerate arcs. If no connecting arc exists, the two node sets define independent flow problems; alternatively, a degenerate artificial root arc may be added.

\sum_i b_i=0
X\text{ denotes the nodes not yet connected to the chosen root}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure constructs a strongly feasible starting tree, or identifies a decomposition over }X\text{ and }\bar X.

children.title: Rooted Tree Structure
children.top_down_role: Parent, depth, plus subtree information for the current network basis.

assumptions_latex: The undirected basic arcs form a spanning tree on node set \(V\).
A root node \(r\in V\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parent map and parent arcs uniquely encode the rooted spanning tree.

notation.meaning: parent of a nonroot node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted representation underlying threaded-tree network-simplex implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient the combinatorial tree toward the fixed root \(r\). For each \(v\neq r\), let \(p(v)\) be the adjacent node on the unique path from \(v\) to \(r\), and store the corresponding parent arc with its original network orientation. Set \(p(r)=r\), \(\operatorname{depth}(r)=0\), and \(\operatorname{depth}(v)=\operatorname{depth}(p(v))+1\). These fields encode every tree path and permit the fundamental cycle of an entering arc to be found by repeatedly moving its endpoints to parents until their paths meet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root, parent pointer, parent arc, and depth at each node encode the tree and support fundamental-cycle path discovery.

children.title: Threaded-List Structure
children.top_down_role: Traversal ordering for efficient access to tree nodes or subtrees.

assumptions_latex: A finite spanning tree is rooted at \(r\).
Children of every node have a fixed local order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each rooted subtree occupies one contiguous interval of the threaded list.

notation.meaning: last preorder node in v's subtree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preorder threading with contiguous-subtree intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: List the nodes in rooted preorder and store \(\operatorname{next}(v)\), the successor of \(v\) in that order, together with \(\operatorname{last}(v)\), the final listed node belonging to the rooted subtree \(S(v)\). Then \(S(v)\) is exactly the contiguous list segment beginning at \(v\) and ending at \(\operatorname{last}(v)\). Iterating \(\operatorname{next}\) enumerates that subtree without searching child lists. Optionally storing the predecessor makes each segment directly detachable and insertable while preserving the order of nodes outside the segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preorder successor and subtree-end pointers make every rooted subtree a contiguous list segment that can be traversed or spliced efficiently.
knowledge_statements.title: Threaded-List Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The preorder interval property is mathematically sound, but the threaded-list representation and detachable-segment implementation claim require an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Initialization of network-simplex threaded-tree lists
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization for both an all-artificial star basis and an arbitrary available basis tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an all-artificial basis whose tree is the star centered at root $r=m$, initialize $p(i)=r$, $\ell(i)=1$, $f(i)=i$, and $n(i)=1$ for every $i\ne r$, while $p(r)=0$, $\ell(r)=0$, $t(r)=1$, $t(i)=i+1$ for $1\le i<m-1$, $t(m-1)=r$, $f(r)=m-1$, and $n(r)=m$. For an arbitrary basis tree, choose a root and perform a depth-first traversal of basic-arc adjacency: when an unvisited neighbor $j$ of $i$ is selected, set $p(j)=i$, $\ell(j)=\ell(i)+1$, and thread $i$ to $j$; at a leaf, backtrack through predecessors to the nearest node with an unvisited successor, thread the completed leaf to that successor, and assign the crossed nodes their final descendant and subtree counts. Terminate after backtracking to $r$ with no unvisited successor, setting the last thread to $r$ and the root's final node to the last visited leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the all-artificial star basis, every nonroot node has the root as parent, level one, subtree size one, and itself as final node; the thread visits the nonroot nodes in order and returns to the root. For a general basis tree, a depth-first traversal assigns parents, levels, and thread links. Whenever a leaf is reached, the procedure backtracks to the nearest node with an unvisited child, completing final-node and subtree-size labels along the backtracked path. It stops when the root has no unvisited child and closes the thread back to the root.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is the spanning tree formed by the current network-simplex basis arcs}.
r\in V(T)\text{ is selected as the root}.
S(i)\text{ records the not-yet-visited basic-arc neighbors of }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure constructs consistent arrays }p,\ell,t,f,n\text{ for the rooted basis tree }T.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Threaded-list representation of a rooted basis tree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predecessor, level, thread, final-node, and subtree-size indices for a rooted spanning tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $T$ be a rooted spanning tree on $m$ nodes with root $r$. For $i\ne r$, $p(i)$ is the parent of $i$ on its unique path to $r$, with $p(r)=0$, and $\ell(i)$ is the number of arcs on that path. Removing $\{i,p(i)\}$ defines the subtree $T_i$ containing $i$, while $T_r=T$. A thread ordering $\tau=(r,t(r),\ldots,t^{m-1}(r),t^m(r)=r)$ is a preorder in which all nodes of every $T_i$ occur consecutively after $i$. Consequently, $T_i=\{i,t(i),\ldots,t^k(i)\}$, where $k$ is maximal such that $\ell(t^j(i))>\ell(i)$ for $1\le j\le k$, and $k=0$ if no such successor exists. The reverse thread satisfies $t_R(i)=j\iff t(j)=i$. If $n(i)=|T_i|$, then the final threaded node of $T_i$ is $f(i)=t^{n(i)-1}(i)$; in particular, a leaf has $n(i)=1$ and $f(i)=i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a rooted spanning tree, the predecessor and level arrays record each node's parent and depth. A cyclic preorder thread is chosen so that every rooted subtree forms one consecutive block. The subtree of a node is therefore recovered by following the thread until the level ceases to exceed that node's level. The reverse thread gives the preceding node, the final array gives the last node in each subtree block, and the size array gives the block's number of nodes; a leaf is its own final node and has size one.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a rooted spanning tree on }m\text{ nodes with root }r.
\tau\text{ is a preorder thread in which each rooted subtree is consecutive.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_i=\{t^j(i):0\le j<n(i)\},\qquad f(i)=t^{n(i)-1}(i).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Threaded-tree update after a network-simplex pivot
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental update of flows, potentials, predecessors, levels, threads, final nodes, and subtree sizes after exchanging basis arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a network-simplex pivot inserts the arc between $p$ and $q$ and removes the tree edge $\{u,v\}$ with $u=p(v)$ and $q\in T_v$. After applying the flow change $\Delta$ along the fundamental cycle, reverse the predecessor links on the stem from $q$ to $v$ and set the new $p(q)=p$, updating the associated $\operatorname{ORIENT}$ and $\operatorname{FLOW}$ entries. Potentials outside $T_v$ remain unchanged; all potentials in $T_v$ receive the same shift, namely $z_{pq}-c_{pq}$ when $(p,q)$ enters and its negative-direction analogue $-(z_{qp}-c_{qp})$ when $(q,p)$ enters. Update $t,\ell,f,n$ by cutting the threaded block for $T_v$, rerooting it at $q$, and grafting it after $p$: if $x=f(p)$ and $y=t(x)$ in the retained tree and $z=f(q)$ in the rerooted subtree, set $t(x)=q$ and $t(z)=y$. Levels in the grafted subtree increase by $1+\ell(p)$ relative to its rerooted levels; ancestor subtree counts decrease when $T_v$ is cut and increase by $|T_v|$ along the ancestor chain of $p$ when it is grafted, while final-node indices are changed exactly on ancestor chains whose former final node was displaced. If $v=q$, rerooting is vacuous. Either component may instead be rerooted and made the upper tree; choosing the component with the shorter rerooting stem reduces the update work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a network-simplex exchange, flows are changed along the fundamental cycle. Parent links are reversed only on the stem from the entering endpoint to the detached subtree root, and the orientation and flow arrays are reassigned accordingly. All node potentials in the detached subtree receive one common shift, while other potentials stay fixed. The subtree's consecutive thread block is cut out, rerooted at the entering endpoint, and grafted below the other endpoint; thread links, levels, final nodes, and subtree sizes are then adjusted on the affected subtree and ancestor chains. No rerooting is needed when the new subtree root already equals the old one, and either side may be chosen as the upper tree, preferably using the shorter stem.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is represented by consistent arrays }p,\ell,t,f,n,\operatorname{ORIENT},\operatorname{FLOW}.
\{u,v\}\text{ is the leaving tree edge with }u=p(v).
q\in T_v\text{ is the endpoint of the entering edge that leads the detached component}.
\Delta\text{ is the flow change determined by the pivot ratio test}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The cut--reroot--graft procedure produces consistent threaded-tree and primal--dual arrays for the new basis tree.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Network-simplex state initialization and pivot-chain tracing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Use of a rooted threaded basis tree to store basic arcs and prepare a network-simplex pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a rooted network-simplex basis tree, each $i\ne r$ uniquely represents the basic arc joining $i$ to $p(i)$. Store its direction in $\operatorname{ORIENT}(i)\in\{+1,-1\}$ and its flow in $\operatorname{FLOW}(i)$. Given the root dual value, compute node duals by preorder traversal because the dual of $p(i)$ is available before that of $i$; compute basic flows by reverse-thread traversal because each processed node balance then contains at most one unknown incident basic flow. For an entering arc joining nodes $p$ and $q$, trace predecessor chains to their first common node $k$: first raise the deeper endpoint to the other's level and then move both endpoints toward the root until they meet. Conducting the minimum-ratio test along these two paths identifies the leaving arc. If the leaving arc joins $u$ and $v$ with $u=p(v)$, deleting it separates the nonroot component as $T_v$; when $q\in T_v$, $q$ is the leading node of the component to be reattached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each nonroot node stores the unique basic tree arc joining it to its parent, together with that arc's orientation and flow. A preorder traversal initializes node duals, and a reverse-thread traversal initializes basic flows from node balances. For an entering arc, the fundamental tree path is found by equalizing the endpoint levels and then following both parent chains to their first common ancestor. A minimum-ratio test along that path yields the leaving arc; deleting a parent edge isolates the corresponding rooted subtree.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a rooted spanning-tree basis with predecessor and level arrays }p(\cdot),\ell(\cdot).
(p,q)\text{ or }(q,p)\text{ is the selected entering arc}.
\text{The leaving tree edge is }\{u,v\}\text{ with }u=p(v).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Preorder and reverse-thread traversals initialize the dual and flow states, and predecessor-chain tracing determines the fundamental cycle and leaving arc.}

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Tree-Basis Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-forest operations supporting network-simplex pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the spanning-tree basis of a capacitated minimum-cost flow problem. Store each tree arc with its orientation, residual capacity, cost, and flow. A pricing query obtains node potentials and path aggregates from the represented forest. When nonbasic arc \(e=(u,v)\) enters, expose the unique \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(T\), compute the residual bottleneck \(\theta\) on the resulting fundamental cycle, augment by \(\theta\), remove a blocking tree arc \(f\), and update the basis by \(T\leftarrow T-f+e\). A dynamic-tree implementation realizes the path query, path augmentation, cut of \(f\), and link of \(e\) without explicitly rebuilding the full tree representation.

Every arc has finite or infinite residual capacity in each admissible direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Arc-Pricing Implementations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost pricing for bounded network-flow arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization network-flow basis, compute node potentials \(p\) satisfying \(p_i-p_j=c_{ij}\) on every basic arc \((i,j)\). For each nonbasic arc define \(\bar c_{ij}=c_{ij}-p_i+p_j\). A lower-bound arc is eligible when \(\bar c_{ij}<0\), and an upper-bound arc is eligible when \(\bar c_{ij}>0\), with its residual direction reversed. Full pricing scans all nonbasic arcs; partial or candidate-list pricing scans a maintained subset and periodically refreshes it. Select an eligible arc according to the implementation rule; if no eligible arc exists after a complete scan, return the current flow as optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing computes reduced costs, selects a bound-compatible improving arc, and certifies optimality only after a complete scan finds none.
assumptions_latex: The current flow is primal feasible.
Basic arcs form a spanning tree and determine node potentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete scan with no eligible arc certifies reduced-cost optimality of the current feasible flow.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Basis Sensitivity Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-basis response to cost and balance perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the nonsingular reduced incidence matrix of a fixed network basis, let \(N\) be the nonbasic reduced incidence matrix, and let \(x_N^0\) contain the nonbasic flows fixed at their active lower or upper bounds. If those bounds remain fixed, then under balances \(b+\Delta b\) and costs \(c_B+\Delta c_B\), \(c_N+\Delta c_N\), the same basis gives \(x_B(\Delta b)=B^{-1}(b+\Delta b-Nx_N^0)\) and potentials \(p(\Delta c_B)=B^{-\mathsf T}(c_B+\Delta c_B)\). Its nonbasic reduced costs are \(\bar c_N(\Delta c)=c_N+\Delta c_N-N^{\mathsf T}p(\Delta c_B)\). The basis remains optimal exactly while the perturbed basic flow respects its bounds and every nonbasic reduced cost has the sign prescribed by that variable's fixed lower- or upper-bound status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed network basis exposes affine flow and potential responses; the balance equations include nonbasic flows fixed at their active bounds, and bound feasibility plus reduced-cost signs delimit the basis optimality region.

The original basis is primal and dual feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Shortest-Path Network Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-simplex specialization of the unit-flow shortest-path model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and arc lengths \(c_{ij}\), formulate a unit minimum-cost \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow with balances \(b_s=1\), \(b_t=-1\), and \(b_v=0\) otherwise. Maintain a feasible tree basis, compute potentials \(p\), and price arcs by \(\bar c_{ij}=c_{ij}-p_i+p_j\). Pivot on an eligible negative-reduced-cost residual arc by augmenting around its fundamental cycle. Stop when every residual arc has nonnegative reduced cost. The resulting unit flow decomposes into an \(s\)-to-\(t\) path plus cycles; removing its cycle components leaves an optimal shortest path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve shortest path as a unit minimum-cost flow, using tree potentials and fundamental-cycle pivots until all residual reduced costs are nonnegative; removing cycle components leaves a shortest path.
assumptions_latex: A feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) path exists.
The unit-flow problem has a finite optimum; in particular, no usable negative-cost directed cycle permits unbounded cost reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Flow Network Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum flow represented as a minimum-cost circulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a capacitated network with source \(s\) and sink \(t\), add a return arc \(e_0=(t,s)\) of cost \(-1\), lower bound \(0\), and capacity at least an upper bound on the maximum-flow value; give every original arc cost \(0\). Let \(y\) be a feasible circulation in the augmented network. Its restriction to the original arcs is a feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow of value \(y_{e_0}\), and its cost is \(-y_{e_0}\). Conversely, every feasible original flow extends to such a circulation by assigning its value to \(e_0\). Therefore bounded network simplex applied to the augmented minimum-cost circulation produces a maximum flow after \(e_0\) is deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-cost return arc converts maximum flow into minimum-cost circulation; the return-arc flow in an optimal circulation equals the maximum-flow value.
assumptions_latex: Original arc capacities are nonnegative.
The return-arc capacity is at least the maximum feasible flow value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(y^*\) is an optimal augmented circulation, then the maximum-flow value is \(y^*_{e_0}=-c^{\mathsf T}y^*\).

children.title: Transportation Simplex
children.top_down_role: Network-simplex interface for bipartite supply-to-demand transportation structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Transportation Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-basis simplex for a balanced transportation tableau.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For supplies \(a_i\), demands \(b_j\), and costs \(c_{ij}\) with \(\sum_i a_i=\sum_j b_j\), maintain a feasible transportation plan whose basic cells form a spanning tree of the origin-destination bipartite graph. Choose potentials satisfying \(u_i+v_j=c_{ij}\) on basic cells and compute \(\bar c_{ij}=c_{ij}-u_i-v_j\). If all nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative, stop. Otherwise insert a negative-reduced-cost cell, alternately add and subtract flow around its unique fundamental cycle, choose the largest step preserving nonnegativity, and delete a zero-valued subtracting cell to restore a tree basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transportation simplex prices nonbasic cells with row-column potentials and pivots by alternating flow around the induced bipartite cycle.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\ge 0\), \(b_j\ge 0\), and total supply equals total demand.
A feasible basic transportation plan is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(\bar c_{ij}\ge 0\) for every nonbasic cell yields a minimum-cost transportation plan.

knowledge_statements.title: Transshipment Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network simplex allowing intermediate nodes with arbitrary balances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a directed network with balances \(b_v\), bounds \(\ell_e\le x_e\le u_e\), costs \(c_e\), and \(\sum_v b_v=0\), maintain a feasible flow whose basic arcs form a spanning tree after standard handling of fixed-bound arcs. Determine node potentials from zero reduced cost on tree arcs. Select a nonbasic residual direction having negative reduced cost, add it to the tree, augment along the induced fundamental cycle until an arc reaches a bound, and remove a blocking arc. Stop after a complete pricing pass finds no improving residual direction; the current transshipment flow is then optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transshipment simplex applies network-simplex tree pricing and cycle pivots while allowing nodes to receive, forward, and dispatch flow.
assumptions_latex: The directed network is connected after ignoring arc orientations.
A feasible bounded transshipment flow exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of a negative-reduced-cost residual direction certifies minimum cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate-Node Modeling Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary between transportation tableaux and general transshipment networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transportation tableau requires a bipartition \(V=O\mathbin{\dot\cup}D\) such that every modeled flow variable is an arc from one origin in \(O\) to one destination in \(D\); no node both receives and dispatches modeled flow. A transshipment network need not admit such a bipartition. For example, the directed cycle \(1\to2\to3\to1\) has an odd underlying cycle and cannot be represented by transportation cells on the same node set. It becomes a transportation model only after a transformation such as splitting nodes or replacing paths by origin-destination columns, which changes the native basis representation and may enlarge the formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transportation tableaux cannot directly represent arbitrary intermediate-node networks; an odd-cycle transshipment network requires node splitting or another reformulation.
assumptions_latex: Transportation variables retain their standard origin-destination incidence interpretation.
No auxiliary node copies or path columns are introduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The network \(1\to2\to3\to1\) lies outside the direct transportation-tableau model class.

notation.meaning: origin and destination parts of a transportation graph

knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Column Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master representation with implicit columns supplied by pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the master linear program \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with a column set too large to enumerate. At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master over \(J_k\), obtaining dual vector \(\pi^k\). Represent every omitted column \(j\notin J_k\) only through a pricing oracle that minimizes \(c_j-(\pi^k)^{\mathsf T}a_j\). If the oracle returns a negative reduced-cost column, append it to \(J_k\) and reoptimize; if its minimum is nonnegative, the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master. Thus delayed columns are materialized only when dual pricing makes them eligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep only a restricted master and generate an omitted column when a pricing oracle finds negative reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: The full master is a minimization problem in equality standard form.
The pricing oracle minimizes reduced cost over every omitted column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_j\{c_j-(\pi^k)^{\mathsf T}a_j\}\ge0\) certifies full-master optimality.

notation.meaning: columns present in the restricted master

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Point Column Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dantzig-Wolfe columns induced by extreme points of a bounded subproblem polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^r:r\in R\}\) be a nonempty bounded polytope and suppose \(x\in P\) enters linking constraints \(Ax=b\) with cost \(c^{\mathsf T}x\). Introduce coefficients \(\lambda_r\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_r=1\) and write \(x=\sum_{r\in R}v^r\lambda_r\). The equivalent master uses column \(Av^r\), objective coefficient \(c^{\mathsf T}v^r\), and convexity coefficient \(1\) for each extreme point \(v^r\). Hence an extreme-point column represents one feasible subproblem pattern together with its linking-resource use and cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded subproblem variable is a convex combination of extreme points, each becoming a master column with linking coefficients and cost.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty bounded polytope.
The subproblem variable appears linearly in linking constraints and the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in P\) if and only if \(x=\sum_r v^r\lambda_r\), \(\sum_r\lambda_r=1\), and \(\lambda_r\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Ray Column Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dantzig-Wolfe columns capturing recession directions of an unbounded subproblem polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a nonempty pointed polyhedron have Minkowski representation \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^r:r\in R\}+\operatorname{cone}\{d^q:q\in Q\}\). Every \(x\in P\) can be written as \(x=\sum_r v^r\lambda_r+\sum_q d^q\mu_q\), where \(\lambda_r\ge0\), \(\sum_r\lambda_r=1\), and \(\mu_q\ge0\). Under linking constraints \(Ax=b\) and cost \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), ray \(d^q\) becomes a master column with linking part \(Ad^q\), objective coefficient \(c^{\mathsf T}d^q\), and convexity-row coefficient \(0\). Ray columns are therefore required whenever recession directions can affect linking feasibility or objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unbounded subproblem, nonnegative extreme-ray weights supplement convex extreme-point weights; ray columns have zero convexity coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty pointed polyhedron.
The listed points and rays generate \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point-and-ray master representation is equivalent to membership in \(P\).

notation.meaning: extreme recession ray indexed by q

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Column-Block Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-angular master representation with independent convexity rows and pricing subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For blocks \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(x^k\in P_k=\operatorname{conv}\{v^{kr}:r\in R_k\}+\operatorname{cone}\{d^{kq}:q\in Q_k\}\), with separable objective \(\sum_k(c_k)^{\mathsf T}x^k\) and coupling constraints \(\sum_k A_kx^k=b\). Represent each block by \(x^k=\sum_r v^{kr}\lambda_{kr}+\sum_q d^{kq}\mu_{kq}\), with \(\sum_r\lambda_{kr}=1\), \(\lambda_{kr}\ge0\), and \(\mu_{kq}\ge0\). The master contains a separate convexity row for every block; point and ray columns from block \(k\) have zero coefficients in all other blocks' convexity rows. Given linking dual \(\pi\) and convexity duals \(\alpha_k\), reduced-cost pricing decomposes into one independent problem over each \(P_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each separable subproblem supplies its own point and ray columns, convexity row, and independent reduced-cost pricing problem within one coupled master.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is block-angular with coupling only through \(\sum_k A_kx^k=b\).
The objective is the separable linear function \(\sum_k(c_k)^{\mathsf T}x^k\).
Each \(P_k\) has the stated point-and-ray representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block-column master is equivalent to the original coupled formulation, and its reduced-cost pricing separates by \(k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decomposition algorithm for multicommodity minimum-cost flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Dantzig–Wolfe/column-generation specialization whose pricing problems are single-commodity capacitated flow LPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a basic feasible solution of the master LP and its basis data $B^{-1}$, $\bar b=B^{-1}(u,\mathbf 1)^\top$, and dual vector $(w,\alpha)=\widehat c_BB^{-1}$. At each iteration, any arc slack $s_{pq}$ with $w_{pq}>0$ is an entering candidate. If $w_{pq}\le0$ for every arc, solve for each commodity $i$ the pricing problem $\max\{(w-c_i)x_i+\alpha_i:Ax_i=b_i,\ 0\le x_i\le u_i\}$. A solution $x_{ik}$ generates an entering column $\lambda_{ik}$ when $(w-c_i)x_{ik}+\alpha_i>0$. If no slack or generated column is eligible, the current master solution is optimal; otherwise pivot using the transformed column $B^{-1}(e_{pq},0)^\top$ for $s_{pq}$ or $B^{-1}(x_{ik},e_i)^\top$ for $\lambda_{ik}$, update the basis and dual data, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a basic feasible master solution, using a two-phase or big-M initialization if needed. A positive arc dual value makes the corresponding slack eligible to enter. When all arc dual values are nonpositive, price columns separately for each commodity by solving a capacitated single-commodity flow problem. A commodity flow enters when its reduced profit is positive. If neither a slack nor a generated flow column is eligible, the master solution is optimal; otherwise perform the appropriate simplex pivot and repeat.
assumptions_latex: \text{The continuous multicommodity minimum-cost-flow LP is expressed in a Dantzig--Wolfe master form.}
\text{A basic feasible master solution is available, possibly after two-phase or big-}M\text{ initialization.}
Ax_i=b_i,\quad 0\le x_i\le u_i\quad\text{defines the feasible flow set for commodity }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\forall(p,q),\ w_{pq}\le0\right]\land\left[\forall i,\ \max_{Ax_i=b_i,\ 0\le x_i\le u_i}\bigl((w-c_i)x_i+\alpha_i\bigr)\le0\right]\Longrightarrow\text{the current master solution is optimal.}

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization problem in equality form with basis matrix \(A_B\) and basic costs \(c_B\).
The basis matrix \(A_B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual-price state is the unique vector \[\pi=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\qquad A_B^{\mathsf T}\pi=c_B.\] For any master column \(a_j\) of cost \(c_j\), its reduced cost is \[\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi.\] Consequently \(\bar c_j=0\) for every \(j\in B\); dual feasibility over a column set \(K\) is equivalent to \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\ge0\) for all \(j\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted-master basis \(B\), the dual-price state is \[\pi:=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\] equivalently \(A_B^{\mathsf T}\pi=c_B\). The reduced cost of any available master column \(a_j\) is \[\bar c_j:=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi.\] Basic reduced costs vanish, and the price vector is dual feasible over a column set \(K\) exactly when \(\bar c_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in K\).

children.title: Pricing Problem
children.top_down_role: Implicit-column search and certification interface; application-specific pricing formulations and solvers belong to their problem chapters.

assumptions_latex: A dual-price vector \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\) is supplied by the current restricted master.
All admissible master columns are indexed by one set \(\Omega\), with column-cost pairs \((a_j,c_j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compute \[j^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in\Omega}\{c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\},\qquad \rho^\star=c_{j^\star}-a_{j^\star}^{\mathsf T}\pi.\] If \(\rho^\star<0\), output \(j^\star\) as an improving column. If \(\rho^\star\ge0\) and the minimum was solved globally, output the bound \(\min_{j\in\Omega}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi)\ge0\) as a no-improving-column certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undecomposed exact reduced-cost search for a minimization master.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Algebra of the Simplex Method p. 108

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\pi\), a single pricing subproblem solves \[j^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in\Omega}\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr),\qquad \rho^\star=c_{j^\star}-a_{j^\star}^{\mathsf T}\pi.\] It returns \(j^\star\) when \(\rho^\star<0\). If the minimum is computed globally and \(\rho^\star\ge0\), it instead certifies that no admissible column has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single pricing subproblem minimizes reduced cost over all admissible columns, returning either a negative-reduced-cost column or, when solved exactly, a nonnegativity certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Single Pricing Subproblem

assumptions_latex: The admissible index set is a finite union \(\Omega=\bigcup_{k=1}^K\Omega_k\), where every admissible column belongs to at least one block.
Each block can minimize \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\) independently for a fixed dual-price vector \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(k=1,\ldots,K\), define \[\rho_k^\star:=\min_{j\in\Omega_k}\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr).\] Then \[\min_{j\in\Omega}\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr)=\min_{1\le k\le K}\rho_k^\star.\] Hence any block with \(\rho_k^\star<0\) supplies an improving column, while exact solutions satisfying \(\rho_k^\star\ge0\) for every \(k\) certify that no improving column exists in \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite block decomposition of the global reduced-cost minimum.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Algebra of the Simplex Method p. 108

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(\Omega=\bigcup_{k=1}^K\Omega_k\), define the block pricing values \[\rho_k^\star:=\min_{j\in\Omega_k}\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr).\] The global pricing value has the representation \[\min_{j\in\Omega}\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr)=\min_{1\le k\le K}\rho_k^\star.\] Thus the blocks may be priced independently; global nonnegativity holds exactly when every exact block minimum is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With block-structured admissible columns, global pricing equals the smallest block pricing value. Any negative block minimum improves the master; all nonnegative exact block minima certify termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Pricing Subproblems

assumptions_latex: The admissible column set \(\Omega\) and reduced-cost function \(r_\pi(j)=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\) are well defined.
The pricing method can return a globally optimal value and an attaining column when the minimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compute \[(j^\star,\rho^\star)\quad\text{with}\quad j^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in\Omega}r_\pi(j),\qquad \rho^\star=r_\pi(j^\star).\] Return \(j^\star\) when \(\rho^\star<0\). Otherwise return the globally valid lower bound \(r_\pi(j)\ge\rho^\star\ge0\) for every \(j\in\Omega\). Exact pricing therefore supports both improving-column discovery and a valid stopping decision.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global pricing oracle with an exact optimality guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Pricing Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive certificate for minimization-form column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the master problem with column set \(J\), let \(r_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\) and \(r^*=\inf_{j\in J}r_j\). An additive inexact-pricing certificate of accuracy \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) consists of a returned index \(\widehat j\in J\) and a certified lower bound \(L\) satisfying \[L\le r^*\le r_{\widehat j},\qquad r_{\widehat j}-L\le\varepsilon.\] If \(r_{\widehat j}<0\), the returned column is improving. If \(L\ge0\), no improving column exists and the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master. When \(L<0\le r_{\widehat j}\), the certificate is inconclusive about exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified bounds bracket the minimum reduced cost within epsilon, proving either an improving column, full optimality, or an unresolved pricing interval.

Reduced costs use the minimization convention \(r_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\).

notation.meaning: Infimum reduced cost over all master columns.
Certified lower bound on the pricing optimum.

children.title: Column Generation as Implicit-Column Revised Simplex

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Retained-column delayed column generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement for a finite-dimensional standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_i c_i x_i:\sum_i A_i x_i=b,\ x\ge0\}\), begin a master iteration from a basic feasible solution. Search all variables for an index \(j\) with \(\bar c_j<0\). If none exists, terminate at an optimal solution. Otherwise choose \(I\) containing every current basic index and \(j\), and solve \(\min\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\ge0\}\) to optimality by simplex, warm-started with the current basis, before repeating global pricing. The set \(I\) may contain only the basis and \(j\), all columns that have ever become basic, or an intermediate retained set that removes long-inactive columns. In the first case the restricted feasible set is at most one-dimensional and is solved in one simplex iteration; retaining every formerly basic column can make \(I\) increasingly large. These variants are special cases of revised simplex. Without degeneracy they terminate finitely; with degeneracy, lexicographic tie breaking prevents cycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each master iteration, globally search for a negative-reduced-cost variable. If none exists, the current basic feasible solution is optimal. Otherwise retain all basic columns, the selected entering column, and optionally other previously generated columns; solve that restricted LP to optimality from the current basis and repeat. Keeping only the basis and entering column requires one simplex iteration, while keeping every formerly basic column can produce a large retained set. As revised-simplex variants, these methods terminate finitely without degeneracy, and lexicographic tie breaking prevents cycling under degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: \text{The original problem is a finite-dimensional LP in standard form with a current basic feasible solution.}
I\supseteq B\cup\{j\},\qquad \bar c_j<0,
\text{The absence of a negative reduced cost is established by examining all variables.}
\text{Each restricted problem is processed to optimality before the next global pricing step.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\forall i,\ \bar c_i\ge0\right)\Rightarrow x\text{ is optimal};\qquad \text{nondegeneracy}\Rightarrow\text{finite termination},\quad \text{while lexicographic tie breaking prevents cycling under degeneracy.}

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Nonbasic Column Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit-column representation used by revised simplex column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be the full column index set, \(R\subseteq J\) the currently generated finite set, and \(B\subseteq R\) the basis indices. The nonbasic space at the current iteration is represented by the disjoint union \[N(R,B)=(R\setminus B)\mathbin{\dot\cup}(J\setminus R).\] Columns in \(R\setminus B\) are stored explicitly and have directly computable reduced costs. Columns in \(J\setminus R\) remain implicit and are accessed through the pricing problem \(\inf_{j\in J\setminus R}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi)\). Adding generated indices enlarges \(R\) and changes this representation without changing the full master column family \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonbasic set combines stored nonbasic columns with ungenerated columns represented implicitly by the pricing oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-started revised-simplex update after adding generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an optimal restricted master on \(R\), its feasible basis \(B\), and new columns indexed by \(K\). Initialize the enlarged problem on \(R\cup K\) by retaining \(B\), setting each new variable to zero, and computing its reduced cost. While some nonbasic column has negative reduced cost, select one by a fixed pivot rule, compute \(d=B^{-1}a_j\), and pivot using the minimum-ratio step \(\min_{i:d_i>0}(x_{B_i}/d_i)\). If no such \(i\) exists, report primal unboundedness. Stop when all explicit nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative; output the resulting optimal basis and solution for the enlarged restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: New columns enter at zero, and revised-simplex pivots reoptimize the enlarged restricted master from the previous feasible basis.
assumptions_latex: The old basis is primal feasible for the restricted master.
Arithmetic and pivot comparisons are exact, with a fixed anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is optimal for the restricted master on \(R\cup K\), unless an unbounded improving ray is detected.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Pricing Dual Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost interface between a restricted master and its pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization master \[\min\left\{\sum_{j\in J}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_jx_j=b,\ x_j\ge0\right\}.\] For a restricted set \(R\subseteq J\), let \(\pi\) be an optimal dual vector of the restricted master. The pricing problem evaluates \[r^*(\pi)=\inf_{j\in J}\bigl(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr).\] A column with negative reduced cost violates the full-master dual inequality \(a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_j\) and can improve the restricted primal objective. Conversely, \(r^*(\pi)\ge0\) makes \(\pi\) feasible for the full dual; together with restricted-master strong duality, this certifies full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-master dual prices parameterize pricing; negative reduced cost finds a violated dual constraint, while nonnegative minimum reduced cost certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an optimal primal-dual pair.
Strong duality applies to the full master when the pricing certificate is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^*(\pi)\ge0\) certifies full dual feasibility and equality of restricted- and full-master optimal values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Max-Flow Pricing for Multiterminal Network-Synthesis Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A network-synthesis specialization of the master–pricing interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider $\min\{\mathbf c^T\mathbf u:(\mathbf a_{ijk})^T\mathbf u\ge r_{ij}\ \forall k,\ \forall\{i,j\}\in T_r,\ \mathbf u\ge0\}$ with $\mathbf c\ge0$, and solve its implicit-column dual by revised simplex. At a multiplier vector $\bar{\mathbf u}\ge0$, pricing for pair $\{i,j\}$ is $r_{ij}-\min_k(\mathbf a_{ijk})^T\bar{\mathbf u}=r_{ij}-f_{ij}$, where $f_{ij}$ is the maximum $i$-$j$ flow under capacities $\bar{\mathbf u}$. If every $f_{ij}\ge r_{ij}$, then $\bar{\mathbf u}$ is optimal; otherwise a minimum-cut column for a violated pair may enter the basis. If some component of $\bar{\mathbf u}$ is negative, its corresponding slack is eligible to enter. With an anti-cycling rule, the simplex-based procedure terminates finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the implicit-column dual by revised simplex. Price columns by maximum-flow/minimum-cut computations under the current capacity multipliers. All tree-pair flows meeting their requirements certify optimality; otherwise add a minimum-cut column for a violated pair and pivot. Negative capacity multipliers are handled by entering the corresponding slack. An anti-cycling rule guarantees finite termination.

\mathbf u\ge\mathbf0
\text{a simplex anti-cycling rule is used for finite termination}

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Master Exact-Pricing Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact column generation under anti-cycling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the full master has a finite column set \(J\), is feasible with finite optimum, and every restricted master is solved exactly by simplex using an anti-cycling pivot rule. At each major iteration, exact pricing returns a column attaining \(\min_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi)\). If this minimum is negative, add an attaining column and reoptimize; otherwise stop. Then the procedure terminates after finitely many simplex pivots and column additions. At termination the restricted solution is optimal for the full master, because the final dual vector satisfies every full-master dual inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many columns, exact pricing, exact reoptimization, and anti-cycling, column generation terminates finitely at a full-master optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite, and the full master is feasible and bounded.
Pricing and restricted-master reoptimization are exact.
A finite anti-cycling simplex rule is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Column generation terminates finitely with a full-master optimal primal-dual pair.
