knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Based Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective bounds derived from a global reduced-cost lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume every feasible full-master solution satisfies \(\sum_{j\in J}x_j=\lambda\) for a known \(\lambda>0\). Let an optimal restricted-master primal-dual pair have value \(z_R=b^{\mathsf T}\pi\), and suppose pricing certifies \(L\le c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\) for every \(j\in J\). For every full-master feasible \(x\), \[c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sum_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi)x_j\ge z_R+\lambda L.\] Since the restricted solution is full-master feasible, the full optimum \(z^*\) obeys \[z_R+\lambda L\le z^*\le z_R.\] Thus pricing supplies a computable lower bound and optimality-gap bound \(z_R-z^*\le-\lambda L\) whenever \(L\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global lower bound on reduced costs converts, under fixed total column weight, into a lower objective bound and computable optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible solution satisfies \(\sum_{j\in J}x_j=\lambda>0\).
The restricted solution is feasible for the full master.
Pricing certifies a global reduced-cost lower bound \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_R+\lambda L\le z^*\le z_R\), and for \(L\le0\), \(z_R-z^*\le-\lambda L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound derivation is internally correct under the strong fixed-total-weight hypothesis, and certificate is the appropriate content kind. No source is supplied, however, and the applicability and standard formulation of this pricing-based bound family depend materially on the master formulation.

children.title: Relaxed Pricing Regime
children.top_down_role: Pricing searches governed by deliberately weakened acceptance requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Pricing Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative sufficient-improvement rule for pricing pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r^*=\min_{j\in J}r_j<0\), and fix \(\theta\in(0,1]\). A relaxed pricing step is admissible when it returns \(\widehat j\in J\) satisfying \[r_{\widehat j}\le \theta r^*<0.\] The returned column need not minimize reduced cost, but it achieves at least the fraction \(\theta\) of the largest available reduced-cost improvement in magnitude. This condition certifies an improving column only; unless the pricing procedure also supplies a valid global lower bound on \(r^*\), failure to find such a column is not a certificate that no negative reduced cost exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed pricing may choose a sufficiently negative but nonoptimal reduced-cost column; unsuccessful search alone cannot certify optimality.
assumptions_latex: The pricing minimum \(r^*\) is attained and negative.
The relaxation parameter satisfies \(0<\theta\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\widehat j}<0\) certifies a valid improving column, but relaxed search alone supplies no stopping certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For negative minimum reduced cost, the inequality correctly expresses a multiplicative sufficient-improvement condition and the stopping limitation is accurate. The condition kind fits the regime leaf, but no source supports this particular relaxed-pricing convention or its terminology.

children.title: Inexact Pricing Regime
children.top_down_role: Pricing searches returning approximate subproblem results.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Pricing Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-accuracy regime for approximate pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r^*=\inf_{j\in J}r_j\). An additive \(\varepsilon\)-inexact pricing oracle returns a feasible column \(\widehat j\in J\) such that \[r^*\le r_{\widehat j}\le r^*+\varepsilon,\qquad \varepsilon\ge0.\] Equivalently, the returned value yields the certified lower bound \(r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon\le r^*\). If \(r_{\widehat j}<0\), the column is improving. If \(r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon\ge0\), no improving column exists. Otherwise the oracle accuracy is insufficient to distinguish full dual feasibility from a missed negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive-error oracle brackets the true pricing optimum; only the bracket endpoints justify improvement or optimality conclusions.
assumptions_latex: The returned column belongs to the full pricing domain \(J\).
The additive error guarantee \(\varepsilon\) is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interval \([r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon,r_{\widehat j}]\) contains \(r^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error inequalities and resulting certification interval are mathematically consistent, and condition is the correct role for the regime. A specialized source is still required to establish that this is the intended inexact-pricing oracle model for the taxonomy leaf.

children.title: Pricing-Accuracy Certification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on convergence or bound claims under nonexact pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Accuracy Certification Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp inference boundary for additive pricing errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose approximate pricing returns \(r_{\widehat j}\) with certified additive error \(\varepsilon\), so that \(r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon\le r^*\le r_{\widehat j}\). Exact full-master optimality is certified precisely when the available lower endpoint is nonnegative: \[r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon\ge0.\] If \(r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon<0\le r_{\widehat j}\), the same reported pair is compatible both with \(r^*\ge0\) and with \(r^*<0\); therefore neither exact optimality nor existence of an improving column follows. Reducing \(\varepsilon\), producing a negative-cost column, or strengthening the lower bound is necessary to cross this certification boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the error interval straddles zero, approximate pricing cannot distinguish optimality from a missed improving column.
assumptions_latex: The only global pricing information is the certified interval \([r_{\widehat j}-\varepsilon,r_{\widehat j}]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact optimality follows iff the certified lower endpoint is nonnegative; a zero-straddling interval is inconclusive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given the explicit assumption that the interval is the only global pricing information, the zero-straddling failure boundary is logically correct and the failure_boundary kind fits exactly. No source is supplied for the specialized certification-boundary formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Termination Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient separation conditions for reliable finite-precision pricing termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume a finite master and a constant \(\gamma>0\) such that every reduced cost relevant to a pricing or pivot decision is either zero or has magnitude at least \(\gamma\). Suppose computed reduced costs satisfy \(|\widehat r_j-r_j|\le\eta\) with \(2\eta<\gamma\), feasibility and ratio decisions are certified consistently, and a deterministic anti-cycling rule resolves exact zeros. Then every nonzero reduced-cost sign is classified correctly by thresholds \(\pm\eta\). Consequently, column generation cannot terminate while a reduced cost below \(-\gamma\) exists, and the induced finite sequence of certified basis changes terminates. A final certificate \(\widehat r_j\ge-\eta\) for all columns implies \(r_j\ge-2\eta\); exact optimality additionally requires a certified nonnegative lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite termination is reliable when numerical errors are smaller than half a uniform decision gap and ties use anti-cycling; exact optimality still needs a nonnegative bound.
assumptions_latex: The full column set and possible bases are finite.
Nonzero decision quantities have uniform separation \(\gamma\).
Certified numerical error satisfies \(2\eta<\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified sign decisions and anti-cycling give finite termination; the terminal solution is at least \(2\eta\)-reduced-cost feasible.

notation.meaning: Uniform separation of nonzero decision quantities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost error implications are plausible, but the finite-termination conclusion depends on a fully specified certified feasibility, ratio-test, pivot-selection, and anti-cycling model. The current statement does not make those numerical mechanisms precise enough, and no finite-precision column-generation source is supplied.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Dual oscillation, tailing-off, and stabilization topics

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-level degeneracy in a restricted master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a restricted master in equality form \(A_Rx_R=b\), \(x_R\ge0\), and let \(B\) be a nonsingular basis with basic vector \(x_B=B^{-1}b\ge0\). The restricted-master basic feasible solution is degenerate when \[x_{B_i}=0\quad\text{for at least one basic index }i.\] Equivalently, fewer than \(m\) basic variables are strictly positive when \(B\) has \(m\) rows. A simplex pivot at such a solution may have zero step length, leaving the primal point and objective value unchanged while changing the basis and possibly the dual prices used by pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-master basis is degenerate when at least one basic variable is zero, allowing zero-length pivots and basis changes without primal progress.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is in equality form with nonnegative variables.
\(B\) is a primal-feasible nonsingular basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy holds iff \(B^{-1}b\) has at least one zero component.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Algebra of the Simplex Method p. 108

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Algebra of the Simplex Method p. 108

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure criterion for restricted-master dual iterates in column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi^k\) be a dual optimum of the restricted master at iteration \(k\), and let \(z_k\) be its objective value. Dual-price oscillation occurs when there exist closed sets \(U,V\subset\mathbb R^m\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(U,V)>0\) and infinitely many indices \(k_1<k_2<\cdots\) such that \(\pi^{k_{2r}}\in U\), \(\pi^{k_{2r+1}}\in V\), while \(|z_{k+1}-z_k|\to0\). Thus objective stabilization does not imply stabilization of the dual prices used by the pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual prices repeatedly move between separated regions even though successive restricted-master objective changes vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi^k\) is selected from the restricted-master dual-optimal set at iteration \(k\).
\(z_k\) is finite for every iteration considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(U,V)>0\), alternating visits occur infinitely often, and \(|z_{k+1}-z_k|\to0\).

notation.meaning: restricted-master dual-price vector at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but this separated-region criterion is a specialized operational definition of dual-price oscillation and has no cited evidence.

children.title: Heading-In Phase
children.top_down_role: Early column-generation progress marked by slow approach toward useful dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Heading-In Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based operational definition of the initial rapid-progress phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization restricted master, fix a window \(w\ge1\) and tolerances \(\tau_z,\tau_r>0\). Define \(D_k=(z_{k-w}-z_k)/\max\{1,|z_{k-w}|\}\) and \(R_k=(\eta_{k-w}-\eta_k)/\max\{1,\eta_{k-w}\}\), where \(\eta_k=\max\{0,-\min_j\bar c_j(\pi^k)\}\). Iteration \(k\) lies in the heading-in phase when \(D_k>\tau_z\) or \(R_k>\tau_r\); over the current window, either the master objective or the worst pricing violation is decreasing materially.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The heading-in phase is a window where the master objective or worst negative reduced cost improves materially.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge w\) and the restricted-master objectives are finite.
\(\bar c_j(\pi^k)\) is available from an exact pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is heading-in exactly when \(D_k>\tau_z\) or \(R_k>\tau_r\).

notation.meaning: relative restricted-master objective improvement over the window
magnitude of the most negative reduced cost
relative pricing-violation reduction over the window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but the windowed thresholds and the particular objective and reduced-cost diagnostics are problem-dependent conventions with no supporting source.

children.title: Tailing-Off Phase
children.top_down_role: Late column-generation progress marked by diminishing improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Tailing-Off Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition separating slow progress from certified termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using window length \(w\), tolerances \(\tau_z,\tau_r>0\), objective progress \(D_k\), and pricing violation \(\eta_k\), iteration \(k\) lies in the tailing-off phase when \(D_k\le\tau_z\), \(|\eta_{k-w}-\eta_k|/\max\{1,\eta_{k-w}\}\le\tau_r\), and \(\eta_k>0\). The first two inequalities express negligible master and pricing progress; the last excludes exact column-generation termination, because a negative-reduced-cost column still exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing off means both objective and pricing progress are small while a negative-reduced-cost column remains.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge w\), and \(D_k\) and \(\eta_k\) use the same diagnostics as the heading-in definition.
Pricing is exact, so \(\eta_k=0\) is a valid termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k\le\tau_z\), \(|\eta_{k-w}-\eta_k|/\max\{1,\eta_{k-w}\}\le\tau_r\), and \(\eta_k>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but the proposed phase criterion lacks a source. It also uses an absolute pricing change, unlike the signed progress measure used by the heading-in definition and classifier.

children.title: Phase-Specific Progress Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable distinctions between early-stage delay plus late-stage stagnation.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Specific Progress Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed classifier for heading-in, tailing-off, and exact termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(w\ge1\), tolerances \(\tau_z,\tau_r>0\), objectives \(z_{k-w},z_k\), dual prices \(\pi^k\), and exact pricing values. Compute \(D_k=(z_{k-w}-z_k)/\max\{1,|z_{k-w}|\}\), \(\eta_t=\max\{0,-\min_j\bar c_j(\pi^t)\}\) for \(t=k-w,k\), and \(R_k=(\eta_{k-w}-\eta_k)/\max\{1,\eta_{k-w}\}\). Output termination if \(\eta_k=0\); heading-in if \(D_k>\tau_z\) or \(R_k>\tau_r\); otherwise output tailing-off.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute windowed objective and pricing progress, then classify the iteration as termination, heading-in, or tailing-off.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization problem and \(z_k\) is nonincreasing.
The pricing oracle returns the global minimum reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule returns exactly one label in \(\{\text{termination},\text{heading-in},\text{tailing-off}\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the diagnostic leaf, but the classifier is unsourced and is not equivalent to the stated tailing-off definition when the pricing violation increases substantially.

children.title: Duplicate Columns
children.top_down_role: Repeated generated columns with identical master-problem representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplication in a linear restricted master, including objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider master columns indexed by \(j\), with constraint vector \(a_j\in\mathbb R^m\) and objective coefficient \(c_j\in\mathbb R\). Distinct indices \(i\ne j\) are duplicate columns when \((a_i,c_i)=(a_j,c_j)\). For every dual vector \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\), their reduced costs are identical: \(\bar c_i(\pi)=c_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}\pi=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi=\bar c_j(\pi)\). Consequently, retaining both variables does not enlarge the master image in constraint-objective space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct variables are duplicates when their constraint columns and objective coefficients coincide; they then have identical reduced costs.
assumptions_latex: The master uses linear equality constraints and linear objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((a_i,c_i)=(a_j,c_j)\Rightarrow \bar c_i(\pi)=\bar c_j(\pi)\) for every \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: reduced cost at dual vector pi

source_refs.locator: 3.6. Column geometry and the simplex method p. 119

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6. Column geometry and the simplex method p. 119

children.title: Symmetric Columns
children.top_down_role: Distinct generated columns related through problem symmetry.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column symmetry induced by a constraint-row group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a group \(G\) act on column indices and let each \(g\in G\) have an invertible row transformation \(Q_g\). Columns \(i\) and \(j\) are symmetric when \(j=g i\) for some \(g\in G\), \(a_{g i}=Q_g a_i\), and \(c_{g i}=c_i\), while \(Q_g b=b\) and the master constraint system is invariant under \(Q_g\). Their orbit \(G i\) is a symmetry class; its members represent equivalent variables under the induced transformation of primal constraints and dual prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric columns belong to one group orbit and become equivalent after a master-preserving row transformation.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on the master column indices.
Each \(Q_g\) preserves the right-hand side and the master constraint system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j\in G i\Rightarrow a_j=Q_g a_i\) and \(c_j=c_i\) for some \(g\in G\).

notation.meaning: symmetry group acting on column indices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but the asserted group-action model and induced equivalence of variables and dual prices require a source and a precise statement of master-system invariance.

children.title: Redundant-Column Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Restricted-master growth caused by duplicate or symmetry-equivalent columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Column Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded master growth without enlargement of its constraint-objective cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted column set \(J_k\), define \(K_k=\operatorname{cone}\{(a_j,c_j):j\in J_k\}\). Redundant-column accumulation occurs when \(|J_k|\to\infty\) along an iteration subsequence but \(K_{k+1}=K_k\) eventually. In particular, every newly admitted column satisfies \((a_j,c_j)=\sum_{i\in J_k}\theta_i(a_i,c_i)\) for coefficients \(\theta_i\ge0\). Such additions enlarge the restricted-master representation and may increase degeneracy or solution time, but do not enlarge its attainable constraint-objective cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted master keeps growing although every new column is conically represented by columns already present.
assumptions_latex: Master variables are nonnegative.
Each new column includes both its constraint vector and objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|J_k|\to\infty\) while \(K_{k+1}=K_k\) eventually.

notation.meaning: restricted-master column set at iteration k
constraint-objective cone generated by the retained columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the cone condition is coherent for nonnegative master variables, but this characterization of accumulation and its degeneracy implications lack cited support.

children.title: Symmetry-Class Column Selection
children.top_down_role: Navigation over representative choices within families of symmetric columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Class Column Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-filtered admission rule for symmetric priced columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a priced candidate set \(C_k\), reduced costs \(\bar c_j(\pi^k)\), a group action \(G\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Partition \(C_k\) into orbits under \(G\). For each orbit \(O\), choose one representative \(j_O\in\arg\min_{j\in O}\bar c_j(\pi^k)\), breaking ties deterministically, and admit \(j_O\) only if \(\bar c_{j_O}(\pi^k)<-\varepsilon\). Output the selected representatives after discarding any representative whose pair \((a_{j_O},c_{j_O})\) already occurs in the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition candidates into symmetry orbits, retain the best negative-reduced-cost representative from each orbit, and reject duplicates.
assumptions_latex: The symmetry action on candidate indices is known.
Reduced costs are comparable within every enumerated orbit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output contains at most one nonduplicate column from each orbit and every output column has reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: priced candidate columns at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the orbit-filtered admission policy is unsourced. Its validity also depends on stronger symmetry and convergence-preservation conditions than the stated comparability assumption.

children.title: Dual-Region Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Restriction of dual iterates to a selected stabilization region.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Region Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic stabilized restricted-master dual update over a controlled region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given restricted columns \(J_k\), a stability center \(\bar\pi^k\), and a closed convex region \(R_k\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) containing \(\bar\pi^k\), solve \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi:a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_j\ (j\in J_k),\ \pi\in R_k\}\). Use an optimizer \(\pi^k\) for pricing. If pricing returns a column with negative reduced cost, add it and update the center or region; otherwise remove the artificial regional restriction and verify pricing at an unrestricted restricted-master dual optimum before declaring termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict dual prices to a convex region for pricing, but remove that restriction before certifying termination.
assumptions_latex: The stabilized regional dual problem attains an optimum.
An exact pricing oracle is available for any supplied dual vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is certified only after unrestricted dual feasibility and nonnegative global reduced costs are verified.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits and the unrestricted final check is important, but the proposed generic stabilization procedure and its center or region updates have no authoritative citation.

children.title: Box Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise bounded stabilization regions around a dual reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise dual box and its equivalent restricted-master primal formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(\ell\le u\). The box-stabilized restricted dual is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi:A_J^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_J,\ \ell\le\pi\le u\}\). Its linear-programming dual is \(\min\{c_J^{\mathsf T}\lambda+u^{\mathsf T}p-\ell^{\mathsf T}q:A_J\lambda+p-q=b,\ \lambda,p,q\ge0\}\). Thus the coordinatewise dual region is represented in the primal by nonnegative residual variables \(p,q\) priced by the upper and lower dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounding every dual coordinate in a box is equivalent to adding priced positive and negative residual variables to the restricted master.
assumptions_latex: \(A_J\), \(b\), \(c_J\), \(\ell\), and \(u\) are finite-dimensional.
The box-stabilized primal or dual is feasible and has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi:A_J^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_J,\ell\le\pi\le u\}=\min\{c_J^{\mathsf T}\lambda+u^{\mathsf T}p-\ell^{\mathsf T}q:A_J\lambda+p-q=b,\lambda,p,q\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: coordinatewise lower and upper dual bounds
positive and negative primal residual variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and displayed finite-dimensional LP dual pair are consistent, but no source with a specific locator supports the box-stabilization formulation.

children.title: Region-Geometry Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of stabilization-region shape relative to dual-price behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Region-Geometry Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility conditions for a dual stabilization region sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence of stabilization regions \((R_k)\) is admissible for exact column generation when every \(R_k\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; the current center satisfies \(\bar\pi^k\in R_k\); and regional restrictions cannot permanently exclude all unrestricted dual optima. A sufficient last condition is nested expansion \(R_k\subseteq R_{k+1}\) with \(\bigcup_k R_k=\mathbb R^m\). Boxes, polyhedra, and weighted norm balls may be selected, but final optimality must be checked without a binding artificial boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose closed convex regions containing their centers and expanding enough that unrestricted dual optima cannot remain permanently excluded.
assumptions_latex: The unrestricted restricted-master dual has at least one optimal solution.
Artificial regional constraints are distinguishable from genuine master-dual constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\ne\varnothing\), \(R_k\) is closed and convex, \(\bar\pi^k\in R_k\), and no unrestricted dual optimum is permanently excluded.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the asserted admissibility conditions and nested-expansion sufficiency for exact column generation require a stabilization reference.

children.title: Penalty Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Dual-price control through penalized departure from a reference region or value.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel representation of a dual penalty and its primal residual cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(\rho>0\), and fix center \(\bar\pi\). The penalty-stabilized restricted dual is \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi-\rho\phi(\pi-\bar\pi):A_J^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_J\}\). Under Fenchel strong duality it equals \(\min_{\lambda\ge0}\{c_J^{\mathsf T}\lambda+\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-A_J\lambda)+\rho\phi^*((b-A_J\lambda)/\rho)\}\). Hence penalizing dual displacement is equivalent to charging a conjugate penalty for restricted-master primal residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex penalty on displacement from a dual center corresponds to a conjugate penalty on primal residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(\rho>0\).
A standard Fenchel qualification holds for the displayed primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{A_J^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_J}\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi-\rho\phi(\pi-\bar\pi)\}=\min_{\lambda\ge0}\{c_J^{\mathsf T}\lambda+\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-A_J\lambda)+\rho\phi^*((b-A_J\lambda)/\rho)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits and the Fenchel-conjugate formula is internally consistent, but the qualification is only described generically and neither the duality formula nor its column-generation specialization is sourced.

children.title: Proximal Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Dual-price regularization through proximity to a selected center.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic proximal stabilization of restricted-master dual prices in column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted dual feasible set \(Y_R=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:A_R^{\mathsf T}y\le c_R\}\), a center \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\), compute \[y^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y_R}\left\{b^{\mathsf T}y-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert y-\bar y\rVert_2^2\right\}.\] Price every unavailable column \(j\) using \(r_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^+\). Add columns with \(r_j<0\), update the center according to the prescribed serious-step rule, and repeat. Terminate only when exact pricing gives \(r_j\ge0\) for every column and the original, unregularized master optimality conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the restricted dual near a reference price, price omitted columns at the stabilized solution, and certify termination only against the original unregularized master.
assumptions_latex: The restricted dual feasible set \(Y_R\) is nonempty.
Exact final pricing is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^+\) is the proximal stabilized price; exact nonnegative reduced costs certify optimality for the original master.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no cited source supports this particular quadratic dual subproblem, serious-step update, or termination formulation. An authoritative stabilized-column-generation source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Regularization-Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavioral regimes associated with weaker or stronger stabilization influence.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of quadratic regularization strength on stabilized dual prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_\rho\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y_R}\{b^{\mathsf T}y-(\rho/2)\lVert y-\bar y\rVert_2^2\}\), the parameter \(\rho\) weights proximity rather than the dual objective. As \(\rho\downarrow0\), every accumulation point of \(y_\rho\), when the maximizers remain bounded, maximizes \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) over \(Y_R\). As \(\rho\uparrow\infty\), \(y_\rho\) converges to the Euclidean projection of \(\bar y\) onto \(Y_R\). Thus small \(\rho\) is weak stabilization and large \(\rho\) is strong stabilization under this parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small penalty coefficients recover restricted-dual optimization; large coefficients force prices toward the feasible point nearest the center.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_R\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty and closed.
The regularized maximizer exists for every \(\rho>0\).
For the zero-strength limit, \(\{y_\rho:0<\rho\le1\}\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\downarrow0\) selects dual maximizers, whereas \(\rho\uparrow\infty\) selects \(\operatorname{proj}_{Y_R}(\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: dual price at regularization strength rho

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches the leaf and the stated limits are plausible under this penalty parameterization, but the parameter convention and limiting claims have no inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Dual-Price Smoothing
children.top_down_role: Reduction of abrupt variation across successive dual-price states.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex averaging of current restricted-master prices with a stabilization center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^k\in\mathbb R^m\) be a newly computed restricted-master dual price, let \(z^k\in\mathbb R^m\) be the current center, and choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\). Form \[\tilde y^k=(1-\alpha_k)z^k+\alpha_k y^k.\] Invoke the pricing oracle at \(\tilde y^k\), generating columns with \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\tilde y^k<0\). Update the restricted master and center, then repeat. Because smoothing can hide violations present at another price, final optimality requires exact pricing and feasibility for an unsmoothed dual candidate of the original master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average the new dual price with a center before pricing, but use an unsmoothed dual candidate for final exact certification.
assumptions_latex: \(y^k,z^k\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(0<\alpha_k\le1\).
The final pricing oracle is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tilde y^k\) is the smoothed pricing vector; it is not by itself an original-master optimality certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The smoothing algorithm fits the leaf, but no source supports the specified update. The certification sentence also needs qualification: a smoothed vector can participate in certification if it itself satisfies full-master dual feasibility and the required primal-dual optimality conditions; being smoothed does not categorically disqualify it.

children.title: Stabilization Center Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of the reference dual state used for centering.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Center Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility conditions for a dual-price stabilization center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), a center \(z^k\in\mathbb R^m\) is admissible when it is finite, belongs to the domain of the stabilization penalty, and is accompanied by a valid original-master dual bound or is explicitly treated only as a heuristic center. If stabilized iterates are constrained to restricted-dual feasibility, additionally require \(A_R^{\mathsf T}z^k\le c_R\). A center used for certification must itself satisfy every full-master inequality \(a_j^{\mathsf T}z^k\le c_j\); otherwise it may guide pricing but cannot certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A center must lie in the penalty domain; feasibility requirements depend on whether it guides pricing, constrains iterates, or certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has data \((A_R,c_R)\).
The stabilization penalty has a specified effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certification by \(z^k\) is valid only if \(a_j^{\mathsf T}z^k\le c_j\) for every full-master column \(j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is suitable, but the record combines heuristic-center admissibility, restricted-dual feasibility, bound validity, and certification without identifying a stabilization variant. In particular, restricted-dual feasibility of the center is not generally implied merely because trial iterates are constrained to be feasible.

children.title: Center-Update Regimes
children.top_down_role: Policies governing when the stabilization center changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Center-Update Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static, averaging, and serious-step updates for stabilization centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After obtaining a trial price \(y^k\), update the center by one declared regime: static, \(z^{k+1}=z^k\); averaging, \(z^{k+1}=(1-\beta_k)z^k+\beta_k y^k\) with \(\beta_k\in(0,1]\); or serious-step, \(z^{k+1}=y^k\) when an accepted merit-improvement test holds and \(z^{k+1}=z^k\) otherwise. Any center carrying a certified bound must be replaced only by a point having an equally valid bound. The regime and acceptance test are fixed before interpreting convergence or stopping behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep the center fixed, average it with a trial price, or replace it only after an accepted serious step.
assumptions_latex: \(z^k,y^k\in\mathbb R^m\).
For averaging, \(0<\beta_k\le1\).
The serious-step merit test is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected rule uniquely determines \(z^{k+1}\) while preserving any explicitly required bound validity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the regimes leaf, but static, averaging, and serious-step rules are combined without a sourced framework or a defined merit test. The asserted preservation requirement for certified bounds also needs variant-specific support.

children.title: Bundle Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Bundle-based control of master-problem dual movement.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle model for a concave column-generation dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be concave. Store evaluated prices \(y^i\), values \(D(y^i)\), and supergradients \(g^i\), and form the upper model \[\widehat D_k(y)=\min_{i\in I_k}\{D(y^i)+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}(y-y^i)\}.\] Given center \(z^k\) and \(\rho_k>0\), compute \(y^{k+1}\) by maximizing \(\widehat D_k(y)-(\rho_k/2)\lVert y-z^k\rVert_2^2\) over the dual domain. Evaluate pricing at \(y^{k+1}\), append its cut, and accept it as the new center only under the declared serious-step test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a proximal piecewise-linear upper model of the concave dual, add the new pricing cut, and update the center after a serious step.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and concave on the trial domain.
Each \(g^i\) is a supergradient of \(D\) at \(y^i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bundle subproblem yields a stabilized trial price and its evaluation supplies a valid new model cut.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The concave supergradient upper model and proximal trial step are internally coherent and algorithm is the correct kind, but their application to column-generation stabilization and the serious-step mechanism require an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Primal–Dual Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization mechanisms that coordinate primal information with dual behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint regularization of restricted-master primal variables and dual prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_R}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c_R\in\mathbb R^{n_R}\) be restricted-master data. Given centers \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^{n_R}\) and \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\) and parameters \(\tau,\rho>0\), compute a saddle point of \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^{n_R}_+}\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\;\mathcal L_{\tau,\rho}(x,y),\qquad \mathcal L_{\tau,\rho}(x,y)=c_R^{\mathsf T}x+y^{\mathsf T}(b-A_Rx)+\frac{\tau}{2}\lVert x-\bar x\rVert_2^2-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert y-\bar y\rVert_2^2.\] Use the dual component for pricing and the primal component for restricted-master recovery. Account explicitly for both regularization terms before claiming feasibility, objective bounds, or optimality for the original master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize in the nonnegative restricted-master primal variables and maximize in the dual prices for a convex-concave regularized saddle problem. Use the resulting dual component for pricing and certify the original master only after accounting for both regularizers.
assumptions_latex: \(A_R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_R}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c_R\in\mathbb R^{n_R}\).
\(\bar x\in\mathbb R^{n_R}\), \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\tau,\rho>0\).
The displayed regularized saddle problem attains a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The saddle point supplies coupled stabilized primal and dual iterates but is not automatically a feasibility or optimality certificate for the original master.

notation.meaning: restricted-master primal variables and dual prices
number of columns in the restricted master

children.title: Bundle–Primal–Dual Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural combinations linking bundle information to primal–dual stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle–Primal–Dual Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling bundle cuts to a regularized primal–dual saddle system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let bundle cut \(i\) be \(D(y^i)+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}(y-y^i)\), and introduce \(\theta\) with \(\theta\le D(y^i)+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}(y-y^i)\) for every \(i\in I_k\). Then maximizing \(\theta-(\rho/2)\lVert y-z\rVert_2^2\) represents the proximal bundle dual step. Coupling is consistent with a primal–dual master only when the multipliers on these cut inequalities are nonnegative, sum to one, and reconstruct the associated aggregate primal object and aggregate supergradient. Pricing adds a column and its corresponding cut data to both representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bundle-cut multipliers form a convex aggregate that must agree with the primal object and dual supergradient used by the coupled stabilized master.
assumptions_latex: The stored affine functions are valid upper cuts of a concave dual function.
The proximal bundle subproblem attains an optimum.
Cut multipliers satisfy the subproblem KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in I_k}\lambda_i=1\), the aggregate \(\sum_i\lambda_i g^i\) links the bundle and primal–dual representations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind, but the claimed reconstruction of an associated primal object is decomposition-specific and that object is not defined. A source must establish the precise correspondence between cut multipliers, primal columns, and supergradients.

children.title: Coupling Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where combined stabilization loses effectiveness or creates conflicting controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which bundle and primal–dual stabilization cease to represent one master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bundle–primal–dual coupling fails as an exact representation if any retained affine function is not a valid global upper cut of the concave dual, if cut multipliers cannot be chosen with \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), or if the aggregate encoded by \(\lambda\) cannot be realized by the restricted primal columns. It also cannot certify the original master while pricing is inexact or omitted columns with \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y<0\) remain. Under any such failure, the stabilized solution is only a heuristic trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalid cuts, inconsistent convex aggregation, unrealizable primal aggregates, or incomplete pricing break exact bundle–primal–dual coupling and prevent certification.
assumptions_latex: A claimed coupling uses bundle cuts and restricted-master primal columns.
Original-master certification requires complete pricing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any listed violation destroys the claimed exact coupling or its original-master optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of omitted column j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, but the listed conditions depend on the particular bundle–primal–dual representation. No citation establishes that they are necessary failure boundaries for the intended decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-pool policy preserving master correctness and reproducibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a pool \(P_k\) of generated columns and an active restricted-master set \(R_k\subseteq P_k\). After pricing at \(y^k\), insert every accepted column \(j\) with metadata \((a_j,c_j,r_j,k)\), where \(r_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y^k\). Activate columns selected by a deterministic reduced-cost and capacity policy; never remove basic columns or columns needed to represent the incumbent primal solution. Evicted columns remain regenerable by exact pricing. Terminate only after full pricing, not merely after finding no improving column in \(P_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store generated columns with pricing metadata, choose an active subset reproducibly, preserve incumbent-support columns, and never substitute pool exhaustion for full pricing.
assumptions_latex: Each stored column has immutable coefficients and cost.
The pricing oracle can regenerate any omitted improving column.
Restricted-master basis membership is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pool operations preserve the incumbent restricted solution, while exact full pricing remains necessary for global termination.

notation.meaning: reduced cost recorded at generation or repricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits column-pool management, but the deterministic activation policy, protected-column requirements, metadata, and regeneration assumptions are implementation choices with no supporting source.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Column Cleanup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe deletion policy for inactive nonbasic restricted-master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active column \(j\), maintain its nonbasic age \(q_j^k\), setting \(q_j^{k+1}=q_j^k+1\) when its primal value is zero and it is nonbasic, and resetting it to zero otherwise. Given an age threshold \(Q\) and reduced-cost margin \(\delta\ge0\), remove \(j\) from the active master only if \(q_j^k\ge Q\), its current reduced cost satisfies \(r_j^k\ge\delta\), and it is neither basic nor protected. Retain enough columns for restricted-master feasibility; deleted columns remain eligible for regeneration by pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only sufficiently old, nonbasic, nonimproving, unprotected columns while preserving restricted-master feasibility and allowing regeneration.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb N\) and \(\delta\ge0\).
Current basis status, primal values, and reduced costs are available.
Deleted columns can be regenerated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cleanup preserves the current feasible basis and does not exclude a deleted column from future pricing.

notation.meaning: consecutive nonbasic-zero age of column j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cleanup algorithm fits the leaf and its safeguards are plausible, but the age-and-margin deletion rule is implementation-dependent and lacks a specifically located authoritative source.

children.title: Pricing Caches
children.top_down_role: Stored pricing information used across restricted-master iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Caches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-tagged storage of reusable pricing-subproblem information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing-cache entry is a tuple \(E=(\sigma,y_0,s_0,V)\), where \(\sigma\) identifies the pricing subproblem and immutable data version, \(y_0\) is the dual vector at creation, \(s_0\) is reusable solver state, and \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is its declared validity region. At a new price \(y\), reuse \(s_0\) only when the current signature equals \(\sigma\) and \(y\in V\); otherwise invalidate or rebuild the entry. Cached bounds may support pruning only when their validity for the current \(y\) is mathematically certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache pricing solver state together with data-version and dual-region validity tags; reuse or prune only when those tags remain valid.
assumptions_latex: Each pricing instance has a stable data-version signature.
Every cached bound records a validity region.
Cache lookup does not alter the pricing objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cache hit is admissible exactly when its signature and declared validity predicate hold for the current pricing call.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the leaf, but the proposed cache tuple and validity region are solver-dependent. The claim that a cache hit is admissible exactly when the two listed predicates hold is too strong unless the signature encodes every solver-state compatibility requirement; a source or a more fully specified cache contract is needed.

children.title: Pricing Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reusable pricing state supplied to subsequent pricing solves.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master problem is a feasible linear program with current dual vector \(\pi\).
The pricing problem minimizes reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\) over admissible columns \(j\in\mathcal J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The warm start is valid only as an initialization; pricing termination still requires a current solve establishing \(\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\bar c_j\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start semantics for repeated exact pricing solves in column generation.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given cached pricing state \(S\) from dual vector \(\pi^0\), initialize the pricing solver for the current vector \(\pi\) with every component of \(S\) that remains feasible for the unchanged pricing domain \(\mathcal J\). Recompute objective-dependent quantities using \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\), continue the pricing algorithm, and return either a column \(j\) with \(\bar c_j<0\) or a valid certificate that \(\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\bar c_j\ge 0\). A cached incumbent or bound alone is not a termination certificate for the new dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse compatible pricing state, recompute all dual-dependent reduced costs, and solve pricing to a fresh improving column or current optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Warm Starts

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic statement is precise and fits the leaf, but the cited delayed-column-generation section does not specifically support pricing-state warm starts, cache compatibility, or transfer of certificates.

children.title: Cache Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Iteration contexts in which retained pricing information remains useful.

assumptions_latex: The pricing feasible region and column encoding are unchanged between calls.
Each cached item records the dual vector and branching or side constraints under which it was produced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact reuse is permitted only when cached feasibility and validity are preserved; otherwise the item may initialize search but cannot certify the current pricing result.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity classes for cached pricing information across repeated master iterations.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached state \(S\) is exactly reusable when its stored feasible objects remain in the current pricing set \(P\) and every stored objective value or bound is recomputed or proven valid for the current dual vector \(\pi\). It is heuristically reusable when it supplies feasible incumbents or search order without supplying a correctness certificate. It is invalid when the column encoding, pricing constraints, or bound assumptions have changed so that cached feasibility or validity cannot be established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cache is exact, heuristic, or invalid according to whether current feasibility and bound validity are preserved, merely useful for initialization, or lost.
knowledge_statements.title: Cache Reuse Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and exact/heuristic/invalid classification fit the container, but this specialized cache-validity taxonomy is not supported by the cited general column-generation section.

children.title: Warm-Start Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Changes in master state or pricing context that limit initialization reuse.

assumptions_latex: A cached state was generated for pricing domain \(P_0\), dual vector \(\pi^0\), and column encoding \(E_0\).
The current call uses \(P_1\), \(\pi^1\), and encoding \(E_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a validity-preserving transfer map, the cached state cannot support an exact pricing certificate for the current call.

notation.meaning: Old and current pricing feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between reusable initialization and invalid transferred pricing certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Transfer of cached pricing state is exact only if a map \(T:P_0\to P_1\) preserves represented columns, feasibility, and every cached bound after objective coefficients are updated from \(\pi^0\) to \(\pi^1\). If no such validity-preserving map is established, or if branching constraints, resource bounds, or encoding semantics change, the cache may at most guide search. In particular, an old claim \(\min_{p\in P_0}\bar c(p;\pi^0)\ge 0\) does not imply \(\min_{p\in P_1}\bar c(p;\pi^1)\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start crosses its exact-transfer boundary when domain, encoding, constraints, or dual-dependent bounds change without a validity-preserving map.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Transfer Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is plausible and internally consistent, but no source supports the asserted validity-preserving transfer-map criterion or its stated boundary cases.

assumptions_latex: The admissible column set is partitioned as \(\mathcal J=\bigcup_{k=1}^q\mathcal J_k\).
Every worker receives the same current dual vector \(\pi\) and current pricing constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global pricing termination is valid exactly when all required workers certify \(z_k\ge 0\), equivalently \(\min_k z_k\ge 0\).

notation.meaning: Pricing partition assigned to worker k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel exact pricing over a partition of candidate columns.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), worker \(k\) solves \(z_k=\min_{j\in\mathcal J_k}\{c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\}\) or returns a valid lower bound attaining the same certification role. The coordinator inserts any returned columns with negative reduced cost. It declares pricing complete only after every required partition reports for the same master version and \(z_k\ge 0\) for all \(k\); stale reports are discarded or recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers price disjoint column subsets against one dual vector; the coordinator accepts improving columns and terminates only after every subset is certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Pricing Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The synchronous partitioned-pricing algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the topic, but the cited delayed-column-generation section does not establish the parallel worker protocol, version consistency, or aggregate termination certificate.

children.title: Column-Generation Chapter Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Interfaces marking where reformulation theory, row generation, or integer search becomes the primary subject.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region decomposes as \(X=\{x:\sum_{k=1}^K A_kx_k=b,\ x_k\in P_k\}\).
Each \(P_k\) is a nonempty polytope represented by its extreme points \(v_{kr}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing boundary for block \(k\) is the minimization of \((c_k-A_k^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x_k\) over \(P_k\), and a negative reduced-cost extreme point supplies a master column.

notation.meaning: Extreme point r of block k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation with equality linking constraints.

source_refs.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Writing \(x_k=\sum_r\lambda_{kr}v_{kr}\), with \(\sum_r\lambda_{kr}=1\) and \(\lambda_{kr}\ge 0\), yields a master whose column \((k,r)\) has linking vector \(A_kv_{kr}\) and cost \(c_k^{\mathsf T}v_{kr}\). For linking dual vector \(\pi\) and convexity dual \(\sigma_k\), its reduced cost is \(c_k^{\mathsf T}v_{kr}-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_kv_{kr}-\sigma_k\). Pricing minimizes this expression over \(v_{kr}\), equivalently over \(x_k\in P_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master combines block extreme points, while pricing minimizes the dual-adjusted block objective and returns an improving extreme-point column.
knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master–Pricing Boundary

source_witnesses.locator: 6.4. Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition p. 239

children.title: Branching Interface
children.top_down_role: Boundary through which branching decisions alter restricted-master structure or pricing.

assumptions_latex: At search node \(t\), branching decisions define a restricted integer-feasible set \(X_t\).
Generated columns encode objects \(p\) from a pricing domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The branching interface is compatible with pricing only when each node decision has a pricing-side predicate that excludes exactly the columns violating \(X_t\).

notation.meaning: Integer-feasible set at search node t.
Pricing predicate induced by node t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility requirement between tree branching decisions and pricing feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every search node \(t\), the branching interface must provide a predicate \(B_t(p)\) such that a generated object \(p\) is admissible at \(t\) exactly when \(B_t(p)=1\). The pricing oracle must optimize reduced cost only over \(P_t=\{p:B_t(p)=1\}\). Branching on a restricted-master variable without a rule applicable to not-yet-generated columns is insufficient, because future pricing could regenerate objects that violate the intended branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching rule is pricing-compatible when it induces enforceable constraints on every existing or future column at the search node.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pricing-compatible branching condition fits the leaf and is plausible, but no source supports the exact predicate formulation or the claim about branching solely on restricted-master variables.

children.title: Nodewise Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing responsibilities local to individual search-tree nodes.

assumptions_latex: Each search node \(t\) has a restricted master and pricing domain \(P_t\).
The restricted master is solved to dual vector \(\pi_t\) before exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node relaxation is solved by column generation only when pricing certifies \(z_t\ge 0\) after all inserted improving columns have been processed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column-generation loop for one branch-and-price search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(t\), solve the current restricted master, obtain \(\pi_t\), and compute \(z_t=\min_{p\in P_t}\bar c(p;\pi_t)\). If \(z_t<0\), insert one or more attaining or improving columns and repeat. If \(z_t\ge 0\) is certified, return the restricted-master solution as the optimal linear relaxation value for node \(t\). A bound or certificate from another node is usable only after validity under \(P_t\) and \(\pi_t\) is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each tree node, repeatedly solve the restricted master and its node-constrained pricing problem until no negative reduced-cost column remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Nodewise Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nodewise column-generation loop and relaxation certificate are coherent, but the branch-and-price-specific formulation has no cited evidence.

children.title: Tree-Level Column Reuse
children.top_down_role: Transfer of generated columns across related search-tree nodes.

assumptions_latex: A column \(p\) was generated at tree node \(s\).
Node \(t\) has pricing predicate \(B_t\) and current dual vector \(\pi_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The column may enter the node-\(t\) master exactly when \(B_t(p)=1\); its reduced cost must be recomputed using \(\pi_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving reuse of generated columns across a branch-and-price tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A column \(p\) generated at node \(s\) is reusable at node \(t\) if its original structural feasibility remains valid and \(B_t(p)=1\). Reuse preserves only the column representation; its reduced cost must be recomputed as \(\bar c(p;\pi_t)\). If \(t\) is a descendant of \(s\), feasibility under the descendant constraints is still checked explicitly. A column infeasible at \(t\) may remain in a global pool but must not be active in the node-\(t\) master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pooled column can be reused at another tree node only after checking that node's branching constraints and recomputing its reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Level Column Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reuse condition appropriately separates structural feasibility from dual-dependent reduced cost, but no source supports the tree-level column-pool rules stated here.

children.title: Integrality Enforcement Boundary
children.top_down_role: Separation between simplex-based column generation and tree-level integrality control.

assumptions_latex: The master variables represent generated columns of an integer optimization model.
Column generation solves only the linear relaxation at each search node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(\min_p\bar c(p;\pi_t)\ge 0\) certifies linear-relaxation optimality, not integrality or global integer optimality.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of priced object p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between linear-relaxation pricing certificates and integer-feasibility enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when exact pricing proves \(\min_p\bar c(p;\pi_t)\ge 0\), the resulting master solution \(\lambda^*\) may be fractional. Integrality must therefore be enforced by branching, valid inequalities, or another integer-search mechanism whose restrictions are propagated to pricing. Termination of column generation at a node certifies only the optimal value of that node's linear relaxation. Global integer optimality additionally requires an integral incumbent and exhaustion or valid bounding of all competing search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing optimality closes a node's linear relaxation only; branching, cuts, and global bounds remain responsible for integer feasibility and optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality Enforcement Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary correctly distinguishes node-relaxation pricing optimality from integer and global optimality, but the branch-and-price claims require a dedicated source.

children.title: Column Generation Scope
children.top_down_role: Responsibilities associated with dynamically introducing master variables.

assumptions_latex: A full linear program has a finite or implicitly indexed column set \(\mathcal J\).
A restricted master contains a subset \(R\subseteq\mathcal J\) and is solved to dual vector \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Column generation ends when exact pricing proves \(\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\bar c_j\ge 0\); otherwise an index with \(\bar c_j<0\) is eligible for addition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scope of delayed column generation for a minimization-form linear program.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Column generation is the iterative enlargement of \(R\subseteq\mathcal J\) by solving the restricted master, obtaining its dual vector \(\pi\), and pricing omitted columns using \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\), with any additional dual terms required by the formulation. Its scope is variable generation: the master row system remains fixed during this operation. For minimization, a column \(j\in\mathcal J\setminus R\) with \(\bar c_j<0\) may improve the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation keeps the master rows fixed while iteratively adding omitted variables whose current reduced costs can improve the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation Scope

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

children.title: Row Generation Scope
children.top_down_role: Responsibilities associated with dynamically introducing master constraints.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation contains a maintained row set \(Q\) drawn from a larger valid family \(\mathcal Q\).
The current solution \(x^*\\) satisfies all rows in \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Row generation ends when separation certifies \(g_q(x^*)\le 0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\); otherwise a violated row is eligible for addition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scope of separation-driven constraint generation with a fixed represented variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Row generation is the iterative enlargement of \(Q\subseteq\mathcal Q\) by solving the current relaxation and separating its solution \(x^*\) over the omitted valid inequalities. If rows are written \(g_q(x)\le 0\), a separator returns some \(q\in\mathcal Q\setminus Q\) with \(g_q(x^*)>0\), or certifies that none exists. Its scope is constraint generation: the represented variable space remains fixed during a pure row-generation step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row generation keeps the represented variables fixed while adding valid constraints violated by the current relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Row Generation Scope

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but it lacks a source and the second assumption contains malformed LaTeX (`\(x^*\\)`). Source support is required before settling the exact separation and termination formulation.

children.title: Pricing–Separation Coordination
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between variable pricing and constraint separation.

assumptions_latex: The maintained master may omit both columns from \(\mathcal J\) and rows from \(\mathcal Q\).
Pricing and separation are exact for the current master state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint termination requires both \(\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\bar c_j\ge 0\) and \(g_q(x^*)\le 0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\) at one mutually consistent master state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination protocol when both variables and constraints are generated dynamically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize maintained sets \(R\subseteq\mathcal J\) and \(Q\subseteq\mathcal Q\). Solve the current master, price omitted columns against its current dual solution, and separate its current primal solution. Add any column with negative reduced cost and any row violated by the current solution, then re-solve because either addition can invalidate the other oracle's previous result. Stop only when, for the same solved master state, pricing certifies \(\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\bar c_j\ge 0\) and separation certifies \(g_q(x^*)\le 0\) for all \(q\in\mathcal Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate master solves, pricing, and separation; after every addition revalidate both sides, and stop only on simultaneous consistent certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing–Separation Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the coordination leaf, but no source establishes that the stated same-state pricing and separation tests suffice under simultaneous row and column generation. Their interaction requires formulation-specific validity conditions.

children.title: Joint Master Evolution
children.top_down_role: Master-problem changes caused by concurrent growth of its variable and constraint spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) define the finite linear program \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Every restricted master encountered has an exact optimal primal-dual pair, and pricing and separation are exact.
Initially selected sets \(R_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(J_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) yield a solvable restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\) and \(J_k\) grow monotonically, and the output satisfies every original row and every original dual column inequality.

notation.meaning: Selected row and column index sets at iteration k.
Restricted-master primal and dual solutions, extended by zero outside their selected index sets.
Reduced cost of original column j relative to the selected-row dual solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact column-and-row generation for a standard-form minimization master.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Algebra of the Simplex Method p. 108
6.4 The Dual Simplex Method p. 277

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), solve \[\min\{c_{J_k}^{\mathsf T}x_{J_k}:A_{R_kJ_k}x_{J_k}\ge b_{R_k},\ x_{J_k}\ge0\}\] and obtain an optimal dual vector \(y_{R_k}^k\ge0\). Extend \(x^k\) and \(y^k\) by zero outside \(J_k\) and \(R_k\). Let \(V_k=\{i:(Ax^k)_i<b_i\}\) and \(P_k=\{j:c_j-A_{R_kj}^{\mathsf T}y_{R_k}^k<0\}\). If \(V_k=P_k=\varnothing\), stop and output \((x^k,y^k)\). Otherwise choose nonempty \(\widehat V_k\subseteq V_k\) whenever \(V_k\ne\varnothing\) and nonempty \(\widehat P_k\subseteq P_k\) whenever \(P_k\ne\varnothing\), set \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cup\widehat V_k\), \(J_{k+1}=J_k\cup\widehat P_k\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the restricted master, add violated original rows and negative-reduced-cost columns, and stop only when neither oracle finds a violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Master Evolution

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Algebra of the Simplex Method p. 108
6.4 The Dual Simplex Method p. 277

children.title: Dual-Sided Generation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of simplex-interface coverage when both master dimensions evolve dynamically.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) define \(P=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(D=\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\).
A restricted master on rows \(R\) and columns \(J\) has an optimal primal-dual pair \((x_J,y_R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extended pair \((x,y)\) is globally primal-dual optimal exactly when both full-system boundary tests hold.

notation.meaning: Restricted-master row and column index sets.
Restricted solutions extended by zero outside J and R, respectively.
Full primal and dual residual vectors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stopping certificate separating the row-feasibility and column-reduced-cost boundaries.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Extend \(x_J\) by \(x_j=0\) for \(j
otin J\), and extend \(y_R\) by \(y_i=0\) for \(i
otin R\). Restricted-master optimality gives \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\), feasibility on \(R\), and nonnegative reduced costs on \(J\). The dual-sided generation certificate consists of the remaining inequalities \[A_{i\cdot}x\ge b_i\quad(i
otin R),\qquad c_j-A_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\quad(j
otin J).\] If both families hold, \(x\) is feasible for \(P\), \(y\) is feasible for \(D\), and their equal objectives certify global optimality. If either family fails, restricted optimality alone is not a global certificate: a violated row must be separated or a negative-reduced-cost column must be priced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global termination requires both boundaries: no omitted row is violated and no omitted column has negative reduced cost. Either one-sided test alone is insufficient.
